correctness.rationale: Polar integration proves the finite-sample threshold. The stationary Gaussian Laplace product and Mellin representation are exact; rescaling t=beta^{-k}u yields an integrable beta-function majorant for k/2<p<(k+1)/2 and the stated sharp coefficient. At p=k/2, a log-coordinate plateau and explicit three-piece integrable majorant yield a single logarithm and its sharp coefficient. All cases, including p<1/2 and the half-integer boundaries, are covered analytically; 25 numerical checks supplement the proof.

value.rationale: RMSprop/Adam learning-rate denominators require reciprocal-moment bounds. This result gives exact growth exponents, explicit coefficients and logarithmic phase boundaries in a natural Gaussian stationary benchmark, demonstrating singularity of the vanishing-memory limit despite complete stationary moment regularization, and an exact contrasting finite-startup cutoff. These are a motivated structural asymptotic classification rather than a routine finite sample computation.
